title: String Length
lesson:
## Strings

Strings are sequences of characters enclosed in quotes.

### Creating Strings
```python
s = "hello"         # double quotes
s = 'hello'         # single quotes (same thing)
s = "She said \"hi\""  # escaped quotes
```

### Useful String Methods
```python
s = "hello world"
print(len(s))           # 11 — length
print(s.upper())        # HELLO WORLD
print(s.lower())        # hello world
print(s.title())        # Hello World
print(s.strip())        # removes leading/trailing whitespace
print(s.replace("world", "python"))  # hello python
print(s.split())        # ['hello', 'world']
print(s.count("l"))     # 3
print(s.find("world"))  # 6  (index where it starts)
```

### String Slicing
```python
s = "Hello, World!"
print(s[0])       # H  (first character)
print(s[-1])      # !  (last character)
print(s[0:5])     # Hello  (index 0 to 4)
print(s[7:])      # World!  (from index 7 to end)
print(s[:5])      # Hello  (from start to index 4)
print(s[::-1])    # !dlroW ,olleH  (reversed)
```

### f-Strings (formatted strings)
```python
name = "Alice"
age = 25
print(f"Hello, {name}! You are {age} years old.")
# Hello, Alice! You are 25 years old.
```

### String Operators
```python
print("Hello" + " " + "World")  # Hello World
print("ha" * 3)                   # hahaha
print("ell" in "hello")           # True
```
